## Security And Operations Review

- The confirmation dialog is a user-safety control, not an authorization boundary. The existing admin middleware, server-side status validation, self-account protection, access transition, and activity logging remain unchanged.
- `application/source/routes/web.php` keeps the status route inside the `admin` middleware group. `AdminMemberController::updateStatus` still limits status values and blocks administrators from disabling their own account.
- Full PHP and focused access tests passed. No route, API, schema, private-file, participant-data rule, secret, or historical activity row changed.
- The screenshot contains synthetic `.test` data only. No credentials, cookies, tokens, private URLs, or real participant data are present.
- Rollback is limited to `application/source/resources/js/pages/admin/members/index.tsx`; no migration or data rollback is required.
- No staging deployment or production change was performed or authorized. Target HTTPS, database, storage, backup, restore, monitoring, and operator evidence remain open under DEP-10 (Gate 1 environment and ownership evidence for credible staging and production planning).
- `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` found 0 production vulnerabilities. A full audit reports one high-severity `js-yaml` advisory in the dev-only ESLint dependency chain; no lockfile or audit-fix change was made. Learn should route this as dependency maintenance, not treat it as production-runtime evidence.
- Measure attempt 2 reran the frontend format, lint, TypeScript, and Vite build checks; the prepared main checkout passed all four. `composer run ci:check` passed ESLint, Prettier, TypeScript, Pint, PHPStan with 0 errors, and 208 PHPUnit tests with 1,792 assertions. `php artisan test --filter=LeadLabAccessTest` passed 73 tests with 787 assertions.
